;Business and economy
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on airlines]]
**[[United Kingdom|UK]]-based airline [[Virgin Atlantic]] declares itself bankrupt and files for [[Chapter 15, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 15]] bankruptcy protection in [[United States District Court for the Southern District of New York|New York]] amid a decline in international flights during the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2020/aug/04/virgin-atlantic-files-for-bankruptcy-as-covid-continues-to-hurt-airlines (''The Guardian'')]  

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Beirut explosions]]
**Several explosions in the [[port of Beirut]], [[Lebanon]], kill more than 70 people, injure more than 4,000 others and send [[shock wave]]s that damage homes as far as 10 kilometers (6 miles) away. [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|Prime Minister]] [[Hassan Diab]], whose wife and daughter are among the injured, declares Wednesday a national [[day of mourning]]. The shockwave was felt in a few nearby countries. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53656220 (BBC News)]
**Finnish diplomats confirm that [[Finland]]'s Embassy in Beirut, located 2km from the port, has been "destroyed". No Finnish casualties are known at this time, according to Deputy Ambassador Aki Kauppinen. Prime Minister [[Sanna Marin]] confirmed the embassy premises have been "badly damaged". [https://newsnowfinland.fi/finland-international/report-finnish-embassy-in-beirut-destroyed-by-blast (Newsnow Finland)]
*Heavy rains cause floods and [[landslide]]s in [[Gapyeong]], [[South Korea]], killing at least 14 people and forcing the evacuation of more than 1,000. The rains have also battered [[China]], [[Thailand]], [[India]] and [[Myanmar]]. Neighboring [[North Korea]] warns of possible floods, while the [[New Zealand government]] reports the deaths of three of its citizens in the South Korean floods. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-southkorea-floods/south-korea-floods-landslides-kill-14-idUSKCN2500AZ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Searchers have located the [[United States Marine Corps]] [[Assault Amphibious Vehicle]] that sank near [[San Clemente Island]], off the coast of [[Southern California]], on 30 July 2020. Eight Marines and one sailor of the [[15th Marine Expeditionary Unit]] from [[Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton]], [[San Diego County]] died in the "ship-to-shore" training exercise. Recovery efforts will begin by the end of the week.  [https://www.nbcsandiego.com/news/local/marine-corps-finds-sunken-aav-remains-of-troops-killed-in-southern-california-training-mishap/2378800/ (NBC San Diego)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
***The [[Philippines]] posts a single-day [[Southeast Asia]]n record, with 6,352 new COVID-19 cases reported in the last 24 hours, as well as 11 deaths. More than 66,000 people have recovered. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/philippines-posts-record-daily-rise-in-coronavirus-cases-could-become-south-east-asias (''The Straits Times'')] [https://mb.com.ph/2020/08/04/10-more-filipinos-abroad-added-to-list-of-covid-19-victims/ (''Manila Bulletin'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
***[[Poland]] reports a single-day record of 680 new cases in the last 24 hours, as well as six deaths. More than a third are in the southern [[Silesia]] region, largely amongst [[coal miner]]s. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/poland-reports-record-increase-covid-cases (Voice of America)]

;Law and crime
*The [[Supreme Court of Justice of Colombia]], in a unanimous decision, orders former [[President of Colombia|President]] [[Álvaro Uribe]] to be placed under [[house arrest]], claiming he may obstruct justice for his fraud and witness tampering case. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-politics/colombia-supreme-court-places-former-president-uribe-under-house-arrest-idUSKCN2502HP?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Thai protests]]
**[[Prime Minister of Thailand|Prime Minister]] [[Prayut Chan-o-cha]] asks people "not to create chaos at this time" as protests grow amid demands to rewrite the [[constitution of Thailand|constitution]], dissolve [[Parliament of Thailand|parliament]], hold new elections and reform the [[monarchy of Thailand|monarchy]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thailand-protests/thai-pm-asks-student-protesters-not-to-create-chaos-idUSKCN2501B7?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[President of Zimbabwe|Zimbabwean President]] [[Emmerson Mnangagwa]] calls his opponents "terrorists" and vows to continue a crackdown on them. In recent days, several opposition members and activists have been arrested and [[human rights in Zimbabwe|human rights]] groups allege that security forces are conducting illegal [[Forced disappearance|abductions]]. Former [[Liberian President]] [[Ellen Johnson Sirleaf]] posted a tweet in favor of the opposition. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/zimbabwe-president-vows-flush-opponents-200804141615075.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Congress of the Republic of Peru]] votes 54–37 [[motion of no confidence|no confidence]] against [[Prime Minister of Peru|Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Cateriano]], forcing all 19 government ministers to resign. [[President of Peru|President]] [[Martín Vizcarra]] has 48 hours to form a new [[Cabinet of Peru|cabinet]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-peru-politics/peru-president-vizcarras-pm-loses-confidence-vote-cabinet-reshuffle-imminent-idUSKCN2501Z4?il=0 (Reuters)]
